written: 2026-11-16, camera PR 5b-i, before any draw of its gates (the composition's share, the cylinder's crease measure, the cylinder on the sampled route against the exact image, the creased derivative)
disclosed: Before the lines were derived, development renders of the cylinder by route 2 at turns 0, 10 and 20 degrees (roll 0, no offset) were made against the exact image while the code was being fixed (a least at the samples' ends read as the side's; the least's place's derivative at the side's medial kink); the derivation (scripts/camera_route2/crease_line.py) reads neither them nor the renderer, and its simulation reproduced the renderer's pixel error at turn 10 to 1e-11 (0.00568987). Those development renders (turns 0, 10 and 20, roll 0, no offset) are not gate evidence: the pinned views (turns 0, 2 and 4, roll 0, no offset; turn 0's view is one of them) hold the controls, and the gate's evidence is the drawn views on fresh seeds.

lines.derivation: scripts/camera_route2/crease_line.py: SAFETY (1.25) times the scan's largest error of the scheme re-implemented on the exact geometry, plus float32's rounding of a sub-ray's point in float32 (camera PR 5a's term)

scan.note: the half-density scan's largest are the same points (turn 0, roll 0 for the pixel; turn 1.5, roll 0 for the motion), so it does not test the factor between the scan's points: the factor 1.25 is a declaration, the space between the points a stated risk the drawn views measure

lines.margin: the factor 1.25 on the scan's largest is declared, not derived: what the lines bound is the scan's 360 poses, measured by an exact numpy re-implementation of the scheme (equal to the renderer's to 1e-11 where both ran); the margin is a declaration for the poses between the scan's points, which the drawn views test; it is never moved after them

third_predictions.written: 2026-11-16, after CAMERA_PLANT=held-least ran (its outcome below), before CAMERA_PLANT=held-caps ran
third_predictions.why: held-least left G17's derivative bit-identical at all four views: the span's least's place reaches the image only where the span's line is the outline (a cap seen edge-on, turns near 0), and there the place's derivative in the body's motion is the axis's tilt in depth times the motion, about sin(turn): zero at turn 0, under 0.07 at turn 4; where the caps open, their outlines hide the span's. It cannot discriminate on the cylinder, so it is no control of this test
third_predictions.g17_derivative_control: CAMERA_PLANT=held-caps (the crease measure's pieces held: values without derivative) fails G17's derivative at turns 4 and 15, where the caps' outlines are the crease pixels' outline, by many times its line; at turns 0 and 2 (caps narrower than two sub-pixels) its outcome is stated per view

march_derivation_finding.written: 2026-11-16, camera PR 5b-i's third agent, after the maintainer's word 'Derive the march term' and before any renderer measurement of the derivative after it
march_derivation_finding.derivation: scripts/camera_route2/crease_march_line.py, output tests/sensing/crease_march_line_pr5b.json: crease_line.py's numpy re-implementation of the scheme on exact geometry, extended with the image's derivative in the body's place along x and z with the held points held (the jvp's) and recomputed with the scheme's discrete choices kept (the rendered image's on its branch), central differences at 1e-4 px (at the two worst poses a quarter and four times that step agree to 0.7 per cent), on the test's aggregates (equivalent radius, centroid) on the crease pixels and the rest; the term is their difference, in px a px of the body's motion; 360 poses (the crease line's), 1053 s on 4 processes
march_derivation_finding.found: on 357 of 360 poses the term is at most 9.8e-5 px a px on the crease pixels (median 2.3e-6, 99th percentile 9.7e-5) and 3.3e-5 on the rest. At three poses it is far larger on the crease pixels: 0.50 (turn 6, roll 75, offset 0.3, 0.8), 0.030 (turn 3, roll 0, offset 0) and 0.024 (turn 2, roll 0, offset 0), all of it at one pixel each, at the rod's end, where a sub-ray passes 0.0013, 0.0010 and 0.0025 px from the side's axis (the march spacing is about 1.1 px). There the span's line is ill-conditioned in both arms (at the first: its distance moves 78 px a px of the body's motion, the sub-cell's share 240 a px) and the jvp's implicit step (the second difference a spacing wide, 5.5e4, against the profile's curvature at the least, 2.4e7) moves the span's place at another rate than the image's held point. The term is narrow in the pose (0.50 at offset u 0.3 px, 0.76 at 0.3005, 7e-6 at 0.302) and not bounded by a scan: a view nearer the alignment can read more
march_derivation_finding.seen_check: a check against numbers already seen, not evidence: at turn 15, roll 20 the simulated term is 5.8e-6 and 6.2e-6 of the crease pixels' motion (x and z) and at turn 4, roll 20 2.8e-7 and 2.5e-7; the first form's measured jvp less the difference there, inferred from its two recorded ratios (3.44 and 0.020 at turn 15, 2.56 and 0.0011 at turn 4), was about 6e-6 and 3.3e-7 of the motion
march_derivation_finding.scan_band: 1.25 times the scan's largest: 0.62 px a px on the crease pixels, 4.1e-5 on the rest; not a bound (above), and as a line it would pass any missing jvp term under about a tenth of the crease pixels' motion (held-caps, at 2800 to 3550 times the 3e-4 line, about 4 to 5 px a px, would still fail by about 7 times)
march_derivation_finding.status: no line committed: the gate's form is put to the maintainer (the coordinator relays). Options: (a) the term derived per view, the line the central difference's own error plus 1.25 times the simulated term at the view itself (the derivation run inside the test, about 8 s a view), confirmed on fresh views with each view's simulated term predicted first; (b) the scan's band, 0.62 px a px on the crease pixels, weak and no bound; (c) the singular pixel fixed first (the span's line and its implicit step where a sub-ray passes near the side's axis), then the band re-derived
